summary: Bidirectional structural deposit-root equivalence is registered as deposit_root_iff: the named Spec SszWitness.Correspondence on well-formed deposits (pinned 48/32/96-byte widths). Construction binds sourceWitness src to sourceNode src at .clValidatorVerifier; determination recovers witness = sourceWitness src from depositVerified witness root with root = sourceNode src. Deposit uniqueness is the named PerfectDepositEncoding (A-PERFECT-HASH) child deposit_unique_of_perfect, not a parent conjunct. sourceNode_mutant_kill_line_refutes_parent is the parent-shaped kill-line (encode mutated to sourceNode + 1; wellFormedDeposit retained). This complements composed_ssz_encoding, which still registers the single traversal conjunct composedEncodingOk on ComposedSszInput (the mutant-exercised deposit-data-root reconstruction under sourceCombine). swapped_combine_kill_line_refutes_parent remains the traversal-child kill-line; inconsistent_witness_kill_line and inconsistent_operation_index_kill_line remain bindOperation-level negatives. SHA-256 functional correctness stays A-SHA256-FFI; the imported Yul fragment stays OPEN under A-YUL-INTERFACE.

theorems.name: LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PSsz1.deposit_root_iff
theorems.doc:
/-- For every well-formed deposit (48/32/96-byte widths), construction binds
`sourceWitness` to `sourceNode` at the CLValidatorVerifier, and determination
recovers that witness from a verified root: the conclusion
`Spec.SszWitness.Correspondence depositSszWitness src` unfolds to
`Construction src ∧ Determination src`.

Bidirectional P-SSZ-1 equivalence at `.clValidatorVerifier`: the named
Spec `SszWitness.Correspondence` (construction binds `sourceWitness src` to
`sourceNode src`; determination recovers that witness). Deposit uniqueness
is the named `PerfectDepositEncoding` / `A-PERFECT-HASH` child
`deposit_unique_of_perfect`, not a parent conjunct. SHA-256 remains opaque
(`A-SHA256-FFI`). Complements the one-object `composed_ssz_encoding`
traversal conjunct. -/
theorems.statement:
theorem deposit_root_iff (src : SourceDepositDataRootInput)
    (hWellFormed : wellFormedDeposit src) :
    Spec.SszWitness.Correspondence depositSszWitness src

theorems.role: registered Verity Executable Contract parent (audit/guarantees.yaml verity.theorem)
theorems.name: LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PSsz1.verity_tx_simulates_ssz_encoding
theorems.doc:
/-- `observe` of the encode transaction equals `sourceView`, and a commit
re-exports the structural witness, `GIndex.concat`, and seven-call digest
conjuncts; a revert restores the snapshot. This is not `SSZ.verifyProof` and
does not prove SHA-256. -/
theorems.statement:
theorem verity_tx_simulates_ssz_encoding
    (input : EncodingInput) (state : Verity.ContractState) :
    ObservesSourceView input state ∧
      CommitPersistsWitnessObservables input state ∧
      ConcatMatchesSpec input ∧
      DigestChainIsExact input ∧
      RevertRestoresSnapshot input state

assumptions.risk: SHA-256 precompile behavior relies on opaque native FFI and host-library behavior; differential vectors do not close this crypto risk.
assumptions.justification: The project proves SSZ preimage shape but does not re-prove SHA-256/precompile functional correctness.
assumptions.violation_impact: Digest-value and proof-verification claims fail if SHA-256 behavior differs.
assumptions.validation: Pin the FFI/precompile interface and run known-answer vectors; do not promote vectors to a cryptographic proof.
assumptions.removal_path: Prove or import a separately certified SHA-256/precompile refinement theorem.

assumptions.risk: The structural deposit encoding `sourceNode` is assumed injective on pinned-width well-formed deposits; without it, determination yields witness equality but not deposit uniqueness.
assumptions.justification: SHA-256 remains opaque (`A-SHA256-FFI`); injectivity of the structural root encoding on well-formed deposits is an explicit hypothesis (`PerfectDepositEncoding`) rather than a cryptographic consequence.
assumptions.violation_impact: Two distinct well-formed deposits could share the same structural root, breaking the unregistered uniqueness child `deposit_unique_of_perfect`. The registered `deposit_root_iff` parent still yields witness equality.
assumptions.validation: Recorded as `PerfectDepositEncoding` in `LidoSRv3.Audit.SszDepositEquivalence` and used only by the unregistered uniqueness child; removal requires a proved injectivity theorem or a narrower deposit model.
assumptions.removal_path: Prove `sourceNode` injective on well-formed deposits from the structural encoding, or refine the deposit model so injectivity is definitional.

assumptions.risk: Multi-node certification transport is accepted as a trust and reproducibility risk; transported results require independent identity and consistency checks.
assumptions.justification: This premise isolates an unproved environment or representation fact instead of hiding it in the theorem.
assumptions.violation_impact: Any guarantee linked to this premise must be re-evaluated if the premise is false.
assumptions.validation: Validated by the linked source spans, executable mutants, or explicit reproduction command where available.
assumptions.removal_path: Replace the premise with a machine-checked correspondence theorem or a narrower proved interface.

assumptions.risk: Pinned solc compilation is trusted when producing bytecode; the project does not prove solc correct.
assumptions.justification: General Yul/EVM correspondence is outside the assurance objective; a pinned compiler is an explicit engineering boundary.
assumptions.violation_impact: A solc miscompilation could break properties of the generated artifact despite correct Lean/Verity proofs.
assumptions.validation: Pin the solc version/profile and retain reproducible artifact hashes when bytecode is produced.
assumptions.removal_path: Adopt a separately verified compiler refinement; not required by the current project objective.

assumptions.risk: Handwritten Yul and direct bytecode require explicit interface composition, not a fabricated source projection.

one-object composition of the four SSZ-encoding children on the single ComposedSszInput.src at the type level: ComposedSszInput.rhs/digestInput/txInput are derived from input.src, so a witness bound for one deposit, an index minted for another operation, or digest bytes for a different deposit cannot be paired with src's pinned deposit-data-root (report/P-SSZ-1.md issue #4's four-child counterexample and issues #20/#21's byte-identity/amount-encoding gaps)

registered parent conclusion predicate composedEncodingOk, stripped in wave 6 to the single mutant-exercised conjunct: the derived witness's traversal to sourceNode src under the source-combine family; the wave-4 conjuncts that unpacked the hBind premise (Ssz.structural_witness_binding_sound), equated the rfl-identical concat artifacts (source_concat_matches_spec), counted the literal seven preimages (digest_preimages_length), unfolded runVerification's definition (accepted_iff_root_matches), and reassembled the width premises (srcInputs_exactWidths) are demoted to unregistered children, still proved and re-bundled on the same one-object input as composedEncodingOkFull (composed_ssz_encoding_full)

parent kill-line: swapped_combine_kill_line_refutes_parent refutes the mutant-substituted parent (composedEncodingOkWithCombine with the model mutant sourceCombineSwapped in place of the honest sourceCombine — the one model function inside the predicate that hBind never mentions) at the concrete swappedCombineKillInput witness where every premise and hBind hold; after the wave-6 strip the mutant-substituted conclusion is exactly the traversal conjunct, which reduces to a Nat.pair tree equality forcing sourceAnchor = 0, contradicting the nonzero public-key fold

conclusion-non-triviality witness: composedEncodingOkFull_not_trivial_crossed_witness (renamed from crossed_witness_kill_line_refutes_parent) shows the unregistered full bundle composedEncodingOkFull is not constantly true (its first structural conjunct fails at the crossed .clProofVerifier operation); the stripped registered predicate mentions neither operation nor combine, so no negation of it is provable, and hBind fails at the crossed point, so this does not refute the parent
